mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months relative to its 12-month moving average compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is continuously active without requiring a threshold crossing.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in periods of declining FEDFUNDS are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5%, it signals a weakening labor market that triggers a flight to quality in equities, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5%, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) over the prior 1 month signals a contraction in the real economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is active whenever both series show negative month-over-month change.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when both INDPRO and HOUST decline, or the Rank IC for the joint signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (defined by FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL > 200), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced liquidity and increased risk aversion. The signal is active only when both conditions are met.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL > 200, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts over the prior 3 months signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is continuously active without requiring a threshold crossing.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in periods of rising HOUST are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts exceed 1650 thousand units, it signals robust consumer spending that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 1650, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decline in the CPI index (CPIAUCSL) over the prior 1 month signals a healthy economic expansion with stable inflation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: labor market strength with stable inflation
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS increases and CPIAUCSL declines, or the Rank IC for the joint signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (defined by GDPC1 above 11550 and RSAFS above 370000), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to overvaluation and potential policy tightening. The signal is active only when both conditions are met.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 > 11550 and RSAFS > 370000, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
